profile.campus: Not a campus. IT1 is a single building at Via Piero Gobetti 96, Arezzo. Aruba operates a second, separate Arezzo facility, IT2, at Via Ramelli 8 a few kilometres away, interconnected by Aruba's own multi fibre cabling on two road routes. The two are a paired site, not one campus.
profile.reading: This is Data Center IT1, one of two Aruba S.p.A. facilities in Arezzo, at Via Piero Gobetti 96 in the Pescaiola industrial zone on the western edge of the city, in Tuscany rather than in Lombardy. That is worth stating at the top, because Aruba's best known site is the Global Cloud Data Center at Ponte San Pietro near Bergamo, which is also the company's registered office, and figures from that campus are routinely and wrongly attached to the Arezzo buildings. The coordinates held for this row sit within about thirty five metres of the Via Gobetti 96 address point, so the address and the outline agree. Aruba S.p.A. was established in 1994 and is headquartered at Via San Clemente 53, Ponte San Pietro in the province of Bergamo. It is the dominant Italian provider of domain registration, hosting and certified electronic mail, and its own company pages claim about sixteen million users, 2.7 million registered domains, 9.8 million managed mailboxes, nine million PEC accounts and around 1 Tbps of internet interconnection, served from seven owned data centres in Europe plus partner sites. Four of the owned sites are Italian. IT1 and IT2 are in Arezzo, IT3 is the Global Cloud Data Center at Ponte San Pietro and IT4 is the Hyper Cloud Data Center in Rome. IT1 itself is a single building of 4,152 square metres total with 1,300 square metres of net data hall, divided into ten islands of seventy racks, each island with its own switch and router. Aruba's own 2025 technical datasheet gives the electrical capacity as 2.5 MW IT, described as redundant, and rates individual racks at up to 40 kW. Those two numbers cannot both apply across the whole floor at once, since seven hundred racks at 40 kW would be an order of magnitude above 2.5 MW, so the per rack figure should be read as what a single rack position can take rather than a density available everywhere. The electrical system is 2N+1 with double conversion static UPS units of 500 kVA giving thirty minutes of standard autonomy and fifteen at minimum, and the batteries and the generators live in buildings separate from the data hall. Standby generation is diesel in 2N redundancy with 48 hours of full load running without refuelling, although Aruba does not publish a megawatt rating for it. Cooling is 2N and mixes chilled water, gas direct expansion with direct dynamic free cooling and an absorption machine, the free cooling being the reason Aruba gives for choosing this climate. Fire suppression uses IG-100 inert gas. The building is certified to ANSI/TIA-942-C-2024 Rating 4, the level formerly called Tier IV, and to ISO 9001, 14001, 27001, 50001, 22301 and 20000-1 among others, and Aruba buys its electricity with Guarantee of Origin certificates. Two points of entrance and two entrance rooms serve a carrier neutral facility. Its reason for being in Arezzo is partly geographic, serving central and southern Italy about an hour from Florence and ten minutes from the A1, and partly architectural, since IT1 is paired with IT2 at Via Ramelli 8 a few kilometres away over Aruba's own multi fibre cables running on two different road routes, giving real time storage replication between two independently sited buildings. On generation, a correction matters. Aruba genuinely does own hydroelectric capacity, eleven plants across Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia totalling about 11.6 MW and producing more than 60 GWh a year, and it has photovoltaic panels across the usable sunlit surfaces of the Bergamo campus. None of that is at Arezzo. The hydro plants sit on the Brembo, Lambro, Astico, Fella and Stura di Lanzo, their output goes into the national grid rather than into a private wire, and Aruba describes it as balancing group demand. So no on site generation figure is recorded for this building. What is not known is substantial. Aruba publishes no utility connection figure, no standby generator rating in megawatts, no PUE and no water figures for IT1, and no year of commissioning. No environmental impact assessment or integrated environmental authorisation for the Arezzo site was found on the national environmental assessment portal, which does carry an Aruba filing for generator sets at the Rome data centre in the Tecnopolo Tiburtino, so the emissions and fuel storage record that exists for those campuses has no visible equivalent here. No tenant is named.
profile.capacity_note: Aruba's own 2025 technical datasheet for IT1 states Total power: 2.5 MW IT (redundant). Because the operator explicitly labels that figure IT, it is recorded as IT load. It is not a grid connection figure and not a total site figure. No utility connection capacity and no megawatt rating for the standby diesel plant are published for Arezzo, so both are left absent rather than inferred from the 2.5 MW. The 40 kW per rack in the same datasheet is a maximum for an individual rack position and cannot describe all seven hundred racks at once, since that would be far above the stated 2.5 MW. Figures of 60 MW and 45 MW that circulate under the Aruba name belong to a different site, the Global Cloud Data Center IT3 at Ponte San Pietro near Bergamo, where Aruba distinguishes them carefully as 45 MW IT power achievable against 60 MW total power. Neither belongs to Arezzo. Aruba's hydroelectric and photovoltaic generation is likewise elsewhere and is generation rather than load, so no on site generation figure is recorded on this row.
profile.research_note: Rebuilt 2026-09-05 from primary sources only. Location verified: this row is Arezzo, Tuscany, not Ponte San Pietro. Stored coordinates fall about 35 metres from the Via Gobetti 96 address point. Capacity taken from Aruba's own IT1 2025 technical datasheet, which labels 2.5 MW as IT. Prior aggregator and encyclopaedia citations removed and replaced with operator documentation.
profile.regulatory_note: No environmental impact assessment or integrated environmental authorisation for the Arezzo site was found on the national environmental assessment portal. That portal does carry an Aruba filing for the installation of generator sets at the Rome data centre in the Tecnopolo Tiburtino, so the absence here is an absence of a national level procedure rather than an absence of searching. Any consent for this building is likely to sit with the Comune di Arezzo and the Provincia di Arezzo and was not located in public form.
profile.onsite_generation_status: None at this site. Aruba owns eleven hydroelectric plants across Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia totalling about 11.6 MW and producing more than 60 GWh a year, on the Brembo, Lambro, Astico, Fella and Stura di Lanzo, and photovoltaic panels covering the usable sunlit surfaces of the Bergamo campus. One of the Brembo plants adjoins the Ponte San Pietro campus. None of this capacity is at Arezzo, and Aruba describes the output as flowing into the national electricity system and helping balance group demand rather than feeding a data centre directly. Electricity at Arezzo IT1 is bought from the grid with Guarantee of Origin renewable certificates.
